title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; the structure is partly known. At the moments when the head is in state C at the right end on a 0, the tape is X(a, b) = (10)^a 1^b C> 0 or Y(a, b) = (10)^a 1^b 0 C> 0. For a large enough, X(a, b) goes to X or Y (by the parity of b) with b′ = f(b) about 3.5b and a′ = a − d(b), with f and d irregular but independent of a (checked for b < 70); the run uses this until a cannot pay, and then the large b is turned back into a (for example X(127, 424) → X(318, 369)). The functions f, d and the turnover are not yet worked out.
Third pass. No halt in 1018 steps (macro simulation). Two inner loops of a round are identified; no pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states exists on either side.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 28,387 cells have been visited and 18,408 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.091).

claims.title: The b-map
claims.text: For a large enough: X(a, b) → X(a−d, f(b)) for even b and Y(a−d, f(b)) for odd b, with (f, d) = (10, 4), (8, 3), (22, 8), (32, 13), (16, 4), (44, 17), (46, 18), … for b = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, … and step counts linear in a; Y behaves the same with f larger by 2 to 4. Checked for b < 70.

claims.title: The run from blank tape
claims.text: C-events include Y(84, 7) → X(71, 40) → X(33, 124) and later Y(322, 7) → X(309, 40) → X(271, 124) → X(127, 424) → X(318, 369) (step 1,168,114); at step 1.5·10<sup>8</sup> the tape is (10)<sup>784</sup> 1<sup>8773</sup>.

claims.title: The b-map, to b < 400, and the X/Y relation
claims.text: For X(a, b) = (10)^a 1^b C> 0 with a large, the next event is X(a−d(b), f(b)) for even b and Y(a−d(b), f(b)) for odd b, the same for two values of a; from Y(a, b) = (10)^a 1^b 0 C> 0 it is exactly Y(a−d(b)−2, f(b)+4) for even b and X(a−d(b), f(b)+2) for odd b. So one function pair (f, d) describes both kinds. Checked for every b < 400.

claims.title: f is digit-driven in base 3
claims.text: For even b, f(b) changes by +12, −6 as the last ternary digit of b/2 goes 0→1→2, with carries contributing amounts that depend on the higher digits: f looks like a 3-regular sequence (computed by a finite automaton reading the ternary digits), which would give it a closed form.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, whole runs of equal blocks crossed at once, exact step counts) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt. At the end the tape is (10)<sup>212,071,119</sup> 101 (011)<sup>71,857,433</sup> 1<sup>30,536,790</sup> …
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA/py/check_msim.py run 1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA 1e18 (macro simulator c/msim.c there, checked against the direct simulator at 109 steps by check_msim.py check)

claims.title: No pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states
claims.text: The pushdown reduction of bb6-1RB0LF_1RC0LB/c/pds.c (one side of the tape kept exactly, the other abstracted by a DFA, reachability by post* saturation) reaches a halt for every DFA with at most 6 states, on either side: TM=1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA ./pds 6 L and R.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: f has no closed form yet, and the turnover when a cannot pay is not mapped.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps two counters at the right end, a block of 10s and a block of 1s; the 1s are pushed through an irregular growth map while the 10s pay for it, and then the roles swap. It has run 109 steps without stopping.

facts.text: No halt in the macro simulator (checked against the direct one at 10<sup>9</sup>).
No halt in the C simulator; 28,387 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Two counters, one paying for the other
html: When the head is in state C at the right end, the tape is a copies of 10 followed by b ones (and sometimes one more 0). As long as a is large, one round sends b to a new value about 3.5 times bigger, by an irregular rule that depends only on b, and lowers a by about a third of the new b.
In the run, b goes 7 → 40 → 124 → 424 twice, each time until a cannot pay any more; then the ones are converted back into 10s and the game restarts with larger numbers.

sections.heading: One map for both kinds of event
html: Write X(a, b) for (10)^a 1^b C> 0 and Y(a, b) for the same with an extra 0 before the head. While a is large, b alone decides what happens: X(a, b) goes to X or Y (by the parity of b) with b′ = f(b) and a′ = a − d(b). Y events need no table of their own: from Y(a, b) the result is the X result with 4 more ones and 2 fewer 10s (even b), or with 2 more ones and the kind swapped (odd b). Checked for every b < 400.
f(b) is about 3.4b but irregular; for even b it moves by +12 and −6 as the last base-3 digit of b/2 steps 0, 1, 2, which points to a rule read off the ternary digits of b.

sections.heading: What is left
html: Find the rule for f(b) (it looks like a digit-by-digit process with period 3 in b/2) and for the turnover, then the halting condition.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.091).
After 109 steps the tape spans 28,387 cells (18,750 left of the start, 61 right), with a density of 1s of 0.648.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: two counters (10)<sup>a</sup> 1<sup>b</sup>: b follows an irregular map while a pays (not yet mapped)
summary: Two counters (10)^a 1^b: b follows a fixed irregular map f (about 3.4b, digit-driven in base 3) while a pays; X and Y events share one table (b < 400). Open.
